live.instructions: Flatre MCP returns scoped Flatre workspace evidence and can request governed internal writes through Flatre Automation when the workspace policy and OAuth grant allow it. Use typed tools for specific record types. Use search_flatre_workspace only when the user wants to search across multiple record types in their Flatre workspace and no record-specific tool fits. Do not provide legal, tax, lending, valuation, fair-housing, negotiation, or brokerage compliance advice. Do not request or infer raw email bodies, raw document contents, attachments, secrets, credentials, direct approval mutations, or direct record mutations. Use prepare_external_email_draft to draft low-risk client or vendor emails for human review. This tool does not send email. Never invoke it for legal, financial, negotiation, wire, inspection-acceptance, or provider-commitment content; direct the user to human review in Flatre instead. General approved guidance is available to authenticated connections without private support-case consent and creates no case. Reading, creating or replying to private support cases requires separate consent. Create or reply to a case only on the user’s request. Support cannot execute account, billing, provider, destructive, or transaction actions. An insufficient_scope result is a permission problem, not an internal tool failure. Present the returned recovery instructions and wait for reconnection before retrying. Do not create a support case as a workaround. Workspace write tools must use stable Flatre target IDs and return Automation proposal, applied, or blocked results; never assume name-only targets. Cite returned Flatre deep links and respect omitted/restricted notes instead of guessing.

tools.name: search_support_guidance

tools.description: Use this when the user needs Flatre support. Find general Flatre product help in the approved guidance catalog. Requires an authenticated connection, not private support-case consent. This does not create a case or diagnose account state. Present applicable guidance verbatim with its citation; a short conversational introduction is allowed. Do not invent fixes or commitments. Every call records security telemetry, including retries.

tools.name: create_support_case
tools.title: Contact Flatre support
tools.description: Use this when the user needs Flatre support. Contact Flatre support when the user asks to report an issue, contact support, or escalate. Creates a private case, may queue private AI support triage, and may send a receipt or eligible support response to their verified email. General how-to questions should use search_support_guidance first. Supply a UUID clientRequestId and reuse it on retries of the same request. Return the saved reference; AI or human replies arrive asynchronously. No attachments or account changes. When presenting a case, include its reference as a clickable Markdown link using the returned href, even when no attachments are involved. Every call records security telemetry, including retries.

tools.name: propose_transaction_update
tools.title: Update or propose transaction fields
tools.description: Requests a replacement for one field on an existing transaction in the user's private Flatre workspace: nextAction, internalNotes, or estimatedCloseAt. The transaction is identified by its stable UUID. The value replaces the selected field rather than appending to it. Eligible changes are executed through Flatre Automation. A routine nextAction replacement can execute immediately with an explicit execution request (reviewOnly=false) and existing Apply low-risk changes consent. Flatre determines eligibility from current member access, transaction permissions, workspace automation settings, record-linked evidence, and the current and requested values; stale field changes are rejected. Sensitive or ambiguous changes remain subject to Flatre review or are blocked. Internal notes, estimated closing dates, reviewOnly=true or omitted, and Prepare changes for review connections are ineligible for immediate execution. This tool does not send messages, approve another action, delete transactions, or change financial, legal, ownership, or compliance fields. The result contains Flatre's processing outcome (applied, proposed, or blocked), a summary, and a Flatre link when available.
